To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Brazil's contributions to international health policy, particularly in the area of access to essential medicines, have been important and relevant.

Brazil has played an important role in the evolution of global essential medicines norms, particularly international human-rights and health policies related to access to essential medicines; Brazil's role in changing global essential medicines norms has had important implications for the AIDS treatment scale-up process in many developing countries; Brazil's role has been particularly important for countries that are currently involved in trade disputes with the United States, such as Thailand and South Africa.

Brazil's efforts to change global norms related to access to essential medicines were important to the development of the global AIDS movement and to improving access to AIDS treatment in developing countries.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is the history of Brazil's role in global essential medicines policy? Why did Brazil choose to pursue a particular approach to global essential medicines policies? What were Brazil's key contributions? How did Brazil's contributions influence global essential medicines policy today? What were the consequences of Brazil's contributions?

the following questions: (1) How did Brazil's efforts to improve access to essential medicines influence global essential medicines policies, particularly in the areas of international human rights, trade and health?

the following questions: (1) Why has Brazil been so important to the international AIDS treatment movement? (2) What are the implications of the Brazilian case for the global AIDS treatment movement? and (3) What are the broader lessons from the Brazilian case for international essential medicines policy?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Brazil's contributions to essential medicines norms have been substantial and important.
Brazil is an essential medicines norm entrepreneur and that Brazil's efforts to change global norms have been successful.
Brazil's efforts to change global norms related to essential medicines have had a significant impact in improving access to AIDS treatment in developing countries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Brazil has played a critical role in changing global essential medicines norms.
the global essential medicines policy has been changing in favour of the access to medicines, but it is still a long way from being achieved.

Brazil's experience with AIDS treatment and its contributions to global policy are a reminder that the international community must continue to push to change the international trade and health policies that impede the global AIDS response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the challenges, Brazil has been able to make important contributions to global health and pharmaceutical policy.

Brazil has been successful in changing global essential medicines norms in part because of its ability to mobilize and leverage the political power of civil society, including the global HIV community.
Brazil's role as a norm entrepreneur is a critical factor that has enabled Brazil to successfully scale up AIDS treatment in the context of globalisation.
